newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly up, gas oil sheds $3-$4.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly up, gas oil sheds $3-$4.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly firmer on Tuesday, traders said.
Gas oil lost $3-$4 a tonne as sliding premiums more than erased modest gains on benchmark IPE futures, traders said.
Good supplies coupled with high shipping costs were limiting interest for fob barrels and the lack of an arbitrage to the Far East removed an outlet for cif cargoes.
Traders said heating oil was around high fob quotes +$2 while Russian could attract no more than high cif quotes +$2.
Algerian gas oil was available at EN590 high cif quotes cif Genoa.
Naphtha was slightly up on light end-user demand and tighter supplies after a 57,000 tonne Skikda cargo moved to the States.
The Bona Fortuna was fixed by Nova for loading February 2 for the U.S. Gulf Coast, shipping sources said.
Gasoline ended slightly higher after a bounce in crude and on continued support from recent U.S. and eastern Med demand.
High sulphur fuel oil was steady, with swaps for February at $91/$92 fob Med. A trader bought Isab material, loading at the beginning of this month, from another trader around $93 fob Med.
Fresh avails are moving in from the east, and are expected to pressure prices.
A trader was heard holding 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil on a larger vessel loading in Rabigh.
A Syrian tender for two 50,000 tonne cargoes of high sulphur fuel closed on Tuesday. Dealers felt this was likely to move into Lebanon.
Low sulphur fuel oil was steady. A trader saw offers at $116 cif Italy. Some of last week's length has now evaporated.
An Italian refiner bought a low sulphur cargo from Scandinavia to cover an end-February requirement.
